ira.name: Provisional IRA / INLA
ira.desc: Irish republican paramilitaries of the Troubles (1969–1998) who fought to end British rule in Northern Ireland through bombings and shootings in Ireland and Britain.

loyal.name: Ulster loyalists (UVF, UDA, LVF)
loyal.desc: Pro-British paramilitary groups in Northern Ireland that killed hundreds of people, most of them Catholic civilians, during the Troubles.

eta.name: ETA
eta.desc: Euskadi Ta Askatasuna, a Basque separatist group that killed over 800 people in Spain and France between 1968 and its dissolution in 2018.

pkk.name: PKK (historical leadership)
pkk.desc: The Kurdistan Workers' Party, founded by Abdullah Öcalan in 1978, which began its armed campaign against Turkey in 1984. Öcalan was captured in 1999 and is serving a life sentence.

asala.name: ASALA / JCAG
asala.desc: Armenian militant groups that assassinated dozens of Turkish diplomats and bombed targets in Europe and Turkey from 1975 to the mid-1980s, including the 1982 Esenboğa airport attack and the 1983 Orly bombing.

eoka.name: EOKA
eoka.desc: Greek Cypriot guerrilla organisation that fought British rule in Cyprus (1955–59) for union with Greece; its successor EOKA-B helped bring about the 1974 coup.

ltte.name: Tamil Tigers (LTTE)
ltte.desc: Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, a separatist army in Sri Lanka (1976–2009) that pioneered suicide bombing and assassinated Indian PM Rajiv Gandhi.

khalistan.name: Babbar Khalsa
khalistan.desc: Sikh separatist group fighting for an independent Khalistan, responsible for the 1985 bombing of Air India Flight 182, which killed 329 people.

chechen.name: Chechen and Caucasus jihadists
chechen.desc: Armed groups of the Chechen wars and the later Caucasus Emirate, behind the 2002 Moscow theatre siege and the 2004 Beslan school massacre.

yb.name: Young Bosnia / Black Hand
yb.desc: Bosnian Serb revolutionaries armed by the Serbian secret society Black Hand; their assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914 triggered the First World War.

imro.name: IMRO
imro.desc: The Internal Macedonian Revolutionary Organization, which in the 1920s–30s carried out assassinations across the Balkans, including the 1934 killing of King Alexander of Yugoslavia in Marseille.

irgun.name: Irgun / Lehi
irgun.desc: Zionist underground groups in British Mandate Palestine (1930s–1948) that bombed and assassinated British and Arab targets, including the 1946 King David Hotel bombing.

nv.name: Narodnaya Volya
nv.desc: 'People's Will', a 19th-century Russian revolutionary organisation that assassinated Tsar Alexander II in 1881.

sr.name: SR Combat Organization
sr.desc: The terrorist wing of Russia's Socialist Revolutionary Party (1902–1911), which assassinated government ministers and a grand duke.

anarch.name: Anarchist 'propaganda of the deed'
anarch.desc: Anarchists of the 1880s–1910s who tried to spark revolution through bombings and assassinations, killing among others a French president, an Italian king, an Austrian empress and a US president.

raf.name: Red Army Faction
raf.desc: West German far-left urban guerrillas (also called the Baader-Meinhof Group), active 1970–1998, known for kidnappings and assassinations of business and state figures. Includes the allied 2 June Movement.

br.name: Red Brigades
br.desc: Italian Marxist-Leninist group of the 'Years of Lead', most notorious for kidnapping and murdering former prime minister Aldo Moro in 1978.

plpac.name: Prima Linea / PAC
plpac.desc: Smaller Italian armed-left groups of the Years of Lead, including Prima Linea and the Armed Proletarians for Communism.

ad.name: Action Directe
ad.desc: French far-left group (1979–1987) that assassinated the head of Renault, Georges Besse, and a senior defence official.

n17.name: 17 November
n17.desc: Greek Marxist group that killed 23 people between 1975 and 2002, including US, British and Turkish diplomats, and went undiscovered for 27 years.

jra.name: Japanese Red Army
jra.desc: Japanese communist militants who allied with Palestinian groups, carried out the 1972 Lod Airport massacre and a string of hijackings and embassy seizures. Includes the United Red Army.

wu.name: Weather Underground
wu.desc: US radical-left group (1969–1977) that bombed government buildings in protest against the Vietnam War.

bla.name: Black Liberation Army
bla.desc: US Black nationalist underground group (1970–1981) that killed police officers and carried out robberies, including the 1981 Brink's robbery.

sla.name: Symbionese Liberation Army
sla.desc: Small US radical group (1973–75) known for murdering an Oakland school superintendent and kidnapping the heiress Patty Hearst.

turkleft.name: Turkish revolutionary left (1970s)
turkleft.desc: The armed left-wing groups of 1970s Turkey (THKO, THKP-C, TKP/ML and Dev-Sol), behind kidnappings, bank robberies and killings; several founders were killed or executed.

sl.name: Shining Path
sl.desc: Sendero Luminoso, a Maoist insurgency in Peru (1980 onward) responsible for tens of thousands of deaths in a war with the state.

mrta.name: MRTA (Túpac Amaru)
mrta.desc: Peruvian Marxist guerrillas who seized the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima in 1996 and held 72 hostages for four months.

farc.name: FARC
farc.desc: Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, a Marxist guerrilla army (1964–2016) that financed itself through kidnapping and the drug trade before a peace deal.

eln.name: ELN
eln.desc: Colombia's National Liberation Army, a Marxist guerrilla group founded in 1964 and influenced by liberation theology.

m19.name: M-19
m19.desc: Colombian urban guerrilla movement (1970–1990) whose 1985 seizure of the Palace of Justice ended with about 100 dead; it later became a political party.

aq.name: Al-Qaeda
aq.desc: Global jihadist network founded by Osama bin Laden in 1988; responsible for the 1998 US embassy bombings and the 11 September 2001 attacks. Includes affiliates such as AQAP and al-Qaeda in Iraq.

isis.name: Islamic State
isis.desc: Jihadist group that declared a 'caliphate' across Iraq and Syria in 2014 and directed or inspired attacks worldwide, including Paris (2015) and Brussels (2016).

ji.name: Jemaah Islamiyah
ji.desc: South-East Asian jihadist network linked to al-Qaeda, responsible for the 2002 Bali bombings that killed 202 people.

boko.name: Boko Haram
boko.desc: Nigerian jihadist group known for mass killings and the 2014 kidnapping of 276 schoolgirls from Chibok.

shabaab.name: al-Shabaab
shabaab.desc: Somali jihadist group allied with al-Qaeda, behind the 2013 Westgate mall attack in Nairobi and the 2017 Mogadishu truck bombing.

let.name: Lashkar-e-Taiba
let.desc: Pakistan-based jihadist group behind the 2008 Mumbai attacks, which killed 166 people.

ttp.name: Pakistani Taliban (TTP)
ttp.desc: Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan, an alliance of militant groups fighting the Pakistani state, responsible for the 2014 Peshawar school massacre.

gia.name: GIA / AQIM
gia.desc: Algerian jihadist groups of the 1990s civil war and their successor, al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb.

eij.name: Egyptian Islamic Jihad / Gama'a
eij.desc: Egyptian militant groups that assassinated President Anwar Sadat in 1981 and carried out the 1997 Luxor massacre.

abusayyaf.name: Abu Sayyaf
abusayyaf.desc: Philippine jihadist group known for kidnappings and beheadings, and for the 2004 SuperFerry 14 bombing that killed 116 people.

hezb.name: Hezbollah
hezb.desc: Lebanese Shia movement and militia backed by Iran, linked to the 1983 Beirut barracks bombings and the 1994 AMIA bombing in Buenos Aires. The US, the EU (its military wing) and others list it as a terrorist organisation.

hamas.name: Hamas
hamas.desc: Palestinian Islamist movement whose armed wing carried out suicide bombings in the 1990s–2000s and the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel. The US, the EU and the UK list it as a terrorist organisation; Turkey and many other countries do not.

pij.name: Palestinian Islamic Jihad
pij.desc: Iran-backed Palestinian militant group founded in 1981, known for suicide bombings in Israel.

pal.name: PFLP / Black September / Abu Nidal
pal.desc: Palestinian militant factions of the 1960s–1990s behind airliner hijackings, the 1972 Munich Olympics massacre and international assassinations.

aum.name: Aum Shinrikyo
aum.desc: Japanese doomsday cult whose members released sarin nerve gas on the Tokyo subway in 1995, killing 14 and injuring thousands.

manson.name: Manson Family
manson.desc: Commune and cult led by Charles Manson, whose members murdered nine people in California in 1969, including the actress Sharon Tate, hoping to start an apocalyptic race war.

temple.name: Peoples Temple
temple.desc: Jim Jones's cult, whose members killed US Congressman Leo Ryan in Guyana in 1978 before more than 900 people died in a mass murder-suicide at Jonestown.

kkk.name: Ku Klux Klan
kkk.desc: White supremacist movement whose members carried out bombings and murders against the US civil rights movement, such as the 1963 Birmingham church bombing that killed four girls.

far.name: Neo-fascist cells (NAR, Ordine Nuovo, NSU)
far.desc: Far-right terror groups in Italy and Germany, from the 1980 Bologna station bombing to the NSU's racist murder series of 2000–2007.
